summary: Adarb1 target-transcript reduction is FDR-significant in only 3 of 22 assayed cell classes, with the clearest engagement in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA, and 052 Pvalb Gaba.
Adarb1 perturbation does not activate a core MDA5/interferon abundance program.
ADAR2-modulating RNA-editing therapies should monitor cytoskeletal mRNAs such as Flnb in addition to intended edit sites and antiviral markers.
The top non-target Ankrd12 responses were almost disjoint across the strongest engaged cell classes.
The buffered, cell-restricted phenotype and absent direct ChEMBL target record make a simple direct ANKRD12-inhibition strategy unsupported.
Mef2c, but not App, drove a multi-gene upper-layer cortical excitatory response among Alzheimer's-linked perturbations.
Top positive and negative whole-dataset signature neighbors based on the nominal non-App tail did not reveal a convincing hidden App module.
The screen supports caution against neuronal ARID1A suppression even though ARID1A loss creates targetable synthetic-lethal cancer states.
Atxn1 did not behave interchangeably with the ataxia-family perturbations Atxn2, Atxn7, or Atxn10.
A restricted Atxn2 top-50 signature connected positively to Dym, Kcnb1, Dyrk1a, Rbfox1, and Fyn perturbations and oppositely to Auts2, Sppl2a, Nefl, Grm3, Cyfip2, and Pten.
Pvalb interneurons and TH Prkcd Grin2c glutamatergic neurons used largely different Bap1 downstream genes.
RNA-level Bap1 target engagement was weak and did not track downstream response size.
No unbiased perturbation was a strong positive or negative Bap1 signature neighbor.
Pcsk1n was the only same-gene nominal response recurring in ten cell classes, usually increasing after Bcl11b perturbation.
Bcl11b resembled Bcl11a, Satb2, and Foxp2 in having no FDR-significant rows, whereas Tbr1 and especially Setd1a produced corrected signatures in the same source matrix.

Bdp1 perturbation produced a multiple-testing-significant response almost exclusively in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut cells, where Ddit3 and six cytosolic aminoacyl-tRNA synthetase genes were induced and Kcnc2 was repressed.
The Bdp1 thalamic signature was a weaker member of a tRNA-handling stress state that is strongest after Elp1 or Elp2 perturbation in the same cell type.
Ddit3 plus cytosolic aminoacyl-tRNA synthetase mRNAs, especially Mars1, are candidate readouts for Bdp1-driven tRNA/amino-acid stress.
The acute Bdp1 response refines Pol III disease expectations to a vulnerable neuronal ISR module rather than simply reproducing the broader Polr3a/Polr3b disease program.
Most Bdp1-assayed cell types showed no FDR-significant downstream mRNA response, but this is better interpreted as weak or unverified target engagement than as true buffering.
Many neuronal classes show little or no FDR-level downstream response to Bmal1 perturbation.
Ndufa13 down-regulation in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut is an exploratory mitochondrial readout of Brd1 perturbation.
L5 ET corticofugal neurons were engaged at the Brinp1 RNA level but had no FDR-significant non-target response.
App self-repression shows that the assay could detect an engaged neuronal disease-neighbor target even though C3 was silent.
C3 had no strong positive or negative all-gene signature neighbor.
Canonical complement-subunit and receptor comparisons around C3 were mostly not testable in the perturbation panel.
Known hippocampal gamma-8 biology did not translate into a preferential CA/dentate transcriptomic response.
Cd247 perturbation lacks measurable on-target transcript depletion in all 22 profiled mouse-brain cell classes.
Published retinal and SLE CD247 biology does not generalize to a detectable non-retinal brain transcriptomic program in this dataset.
The Cd3d target transcript did not show rank-based knockdown in the measured Cd3d cells.
No robust Cd3d-response biomarker emerged; the largest nominal genes were isolated or directionally mixed.
CD3D disease biology is not reproduced in this neuronal Perturb-seq context.
Mouse neural progenitor literature on p16Ink4a/p19Arf does not translate into a broad mature-neuron Cdkn2a transcriptional phenotype in this dataset.
No positive or inverse whole-panel signature neighbor was strong enough to nominate a Cep164 modifier or rescue direction.
Champ1 did not induce a coherent same-direction cross-class module; Gaa was the most recurrent nominal gene and was down in eight classes only nominally.
This Champ1 perturbation does not nominate a corrected downstream biomarker or therapeutic rescue direction.
Chd4 was not phenocopied by Gatad2b or Mbd2 perturbation in the same 151 thalamic cells.
Whole-signature neighbor analysis in 151 did not identify an inverse or obviously antagonistic Chd4 comparator.
A smaller cortical intratelencephalic response centers on Scg-family and Cbln4 upregulation.
Seventeen Cntnap1 cell classes lacked both FDR-significant target knockdown and FDR-significant downstream genes.
The leading raw downstream rows, especially Grin1 and Atp6v0a2 in L5 ET neurons, are exploratory sentinel candidates rather than validated Cplx2 targets.
Pdcd4 is an exploratory repeated positive marker in three telencephalic glutamatergic Dcaf17 signatures, whereas several other recurrent nominal genes flip sign across classes.
Dmxl2 was present as a neuroendocrine disease comparator and showed stronger nominal self-transcript reduction than Dcaf17, but it did not produce a broad corrected program resembling Dcaf17.

Dcaf8 target-transcript knockdown was genome-wide significant only in 155 MB Glut, while six other neuronal classes showed only nominal target depletion and fifteen tested classes did not reach nominal target engagement.
The engaged 155 MB Glut response was almost entirely a self-effect on Dcaf8 mRNA, with no non-target gene reaching FDR<0.05 despite the known role of DCAF8 as a CUL4-DDB1 substrate receptor.
The human DCAF8 axonal-neuropathy mechanism did not appear as a neurofilament-like acute CNS transcriptional program in this dataset.
Therapeutic CRL4A-DCAF8 antagonism should not infer neuronal safety from this buffered mRNA signature alone.
CTX-CGE and CB GABA contained nominal migration-neighbor or cytoskeletal rows despite little or no Dcx transcript engagement.
Eef1a1 did not show detectable mRNA compensation after Eef1a2 knockdown.
The neutral En1 Perturb-seq readout should not be interpreted as evidence that reducing En1 activity is safe or beneficial.
Craniosynostosis-associated transcription-factor perturbations Tcf12 and Twist1 were not directionally interchangeable with Erf in the restricted brain signatures.
The absent Ffar1 self-targeting signal contrasts with detectable on-target knockdown for several available Gq/PLC or downstream signaling neighbors.
The screen supplies little CNS therapeutic-direction information for FFAR1 agonism or antagonism.
Glra1 perturbation produced a single adjusted hit, Slc5a3 down, confined to 054 CNU-MGE GABA cells.
Most Glra1 perturbation contrasts were either weakly engaged or transcriptionally buffered.
The only adjusted Glra1 response arose outside the canonical hindbrain and brainstem-enriched GLRA1 context.
Slc5a3 is a low-confidence candidate biomarker linking the Glra1 perturbation to myo-inositol/osmolyte biology in CNU-MGE GABA cells.
Top Glra1 signature neighbors were too weak to support a convergent transcriptional module.
Glra2 perturbation did not produce a corrected transcriptional response in any assayed mouse-brain cell class.
Glra2 on-target depletion was only nominal and was concentrated in thalamic, midbrain, and hypothalamic classes rather than cortical projection-neuron classes.
Pfkp, Mpp3, Nr2f1, Kcnmb4, and Use1 are nominal single-context leads rather than robust Glra2 biomarkers.
Glra3 perturbation produced no FDR-resolved on-target depletion and no FDR-resolved downstream gene in any measured mouse-brain cell class.
The apparent Glra3 peaks in 066 CNU-HYa HY GABA and 022 L5 ET CTX Glut are only nominal and do not define a robust selective cell-type response.
Gls mRNA itself is the only robust biomarker of successful Gls perturbation in this dataset.
The MB Dopa Grid1 row is too small and too weakly engaged to test the published dopaminergic GluD1 burst-firing mechanism.
The only related-target convergence hint was restricted to 308 CB GABA, where the weak Grid2 signature correlated with Gria4 and Neo1 perturbations.
A full within-cell signature-neighbor search found no reproducible high-correlation positive or negative partner for Grid2.
Several cell types showed statistically clear Hnrnpu target-transcript increase but almost no FDR-level downstream response.
The dataset supports Hnrnpu dosage sensitivity in neurons but warns that increasing Hnrnpu transcript is not automatically equivalent to rescuing HNRNPU loss-of-function disease.
Ifnar1 loss produced a globally buffered transcriptional phenotype: no assayed cell type contained an FDR-significant gene and the target transcript itself was only weakly reduced.
The canonical IFNAR-JAK/STAT antiviral module was not detectably repressed after Ifnar1 perturbation.
CA3-family glutamatergic and CNU-MGE GABA neurons carried the densest nominal Ifnar1 tails, but the genes were noncanonical and did not reach FDR significance.
The muted neuronal phenotype should not be read as evidence that IFNAR1 inhibition is biologically inert or uniformly safe.
The apparent Pvalb enrichment was nominal and the broader Ifnar2 nominal tail was not directionally recurrent.
Zfp532 is an exploratory recurrent positive marker of Kdm5c perturbation, with nominal p<0.01 in six cell classes but FDR support only in 151.
The canonical immune KLF13-CCL5 axis is not detectably engaged by Klf13 perturbation in the strongest neuronal class.
The full panel contained no strong positive or negative Mapk1 signature neighbor.
Loss-of-transcript buffering should not be read as evidence against gain-of-function MAPK1 neurodevelopmental disease biology.
Scn5a RNA induction was not detected in any adult Myt1l-perturbed class, unlike a published SCN5A-linked lamotrigine rescue model.
Lancl1, Nt5c3, Gpr21, and Micu3 were the best non-target nominal rows but remain exploratory NCAM1-response biomarker candidates.
Several Ndufb9-negative cell classes are statistically unresolved because target engagement was nominal, near-threshold, low-count, or absent.
The negative Ndufs4 Perturb-seq result should not be used to deprioritize NDUFS4 disease biology or therapies such as mTOR modulation without first confirming stronger Ndufs4 loss of function.
The nearest neurofilament and neuronal intermediate-filament partners are not induced after Nefh perturbation.
The published hippocampal Ngn3 neuritogenesis branch was not recovered at FDR: Fmn1 and Kif21b stayed non-significant despite prior links to Ngn3-dependent neuronal morphology.
The Bambi response did not behave like a generic BMP/TGF-beta receptor-Smad knockdown state.
Multiple inhibitory or small cell classes with nominal Nfic knockdown lacked an FDR-supported transcriptome response.
The thalamic Nr1d1 clock signature flags Npas2, Cry2, Dbp, and Nfil3 as neuronal biomarkers to monitor during REV-ERB pharmacology.
The weak differentiated-brain response refines developmental Nr2c1 literature toward a progenitor-biased sensitive context.
Hmg20b, a BRAF-HDAC complex transcript, was nominally induced in the strongest thalamic Phf21a response.
The screen sampled neuronal Polr3b sensitivity but did not assay the oligodendrocyte-lineage context central to POLR3-related hypomyelinating leukodystrophy.
Srsf1 was the strongest same-direction perturbation match to the corrected Col4a2/Col4a1/H2ac25 triad in 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut.
Known Tau, Cdk5, and PP2A transcript markers did not move as a coordinated FDR-level module after Ppp2r2b perturbation.
Ppp2r5d target-transcript engagement was concentrated in caudal and posterior neuronal classes and reached FDR < 0.05 only in 191 MB P MY GABA.
191 MB P MY GABA showed clear Ppp2r5d mRNA depletion with no FDR-significant non-target transcript.
Ppp2r5d mRNA itself was the only transcript to recur across at least three classes at p < 0.001; the few non-target leads were class-specific.
A global signature-neighbor search found no strong phenocopy or inverse perturbation for Ppp2r5d.
A published cerebellar mGluR1/PLCbeta4/PKC-alpha LTD mechanism did not appear as a resting Prkca transcriptional signature in 308 CB GABA cells.
The mouse-brain single-cell RNA response does not reveal a broad RAC1 neurodevelopmental-disease module.
The Rai1 Perturb-seq signatures are a weak loss-of-function readout, whereas Smith-Magenis rescue literature points toward Rai1 activation or restoration.
Slitrk6 and Grik1 are candidate Rai1-response biomarkers for 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut but not for all neuronal classes.
The measured brain response did not engage a Reg-family output or compensation program.
The Rest null should not be interpreted as evidence that REST inhibition is neutral for aging or Alzheimer-relevant neurons.
Rnpc3 knockdown did not induce mRNA-level compensation of measured minor-spliceosome-associated factors Pdcd7, Snrnp25, Snrnp35, Snrnp48, Zcrb1, or Zrsr2.
The classes with no FDR-level response also had weak Rnpc3 transcript engagement, so they should be treated as under-engaged negative results rather than as evidence of true resistance.
046 CTX-CGE GABA was the only Rpgr stratum with a sub-0.2 adjusted p value, pairing nominal Rpgr self-decrease with nominal Apc downregulation.
B9d1, unlike Rpgr, generated a corrected 308 CB GABA signature.
The dataset refines RYK neural-development literature by showing no robust adult mouse-brain transcriptional response in the assayed neuronal classes.
Safe_target_11 did not elicit a detectable p53 or DNA-damage transcriptional module.
Top positive and negative whole-signature neighbors of Safe_target_11 were essentially uncorrelated.
Restricted signature-neighbor analysis did not reveal a strong hidden partner or inverse signature.
Safe_target_13 should not be assigned target biology, druggability, disease direction, or a biomarker mechanism from this dataset.
Safe_target_23 has no strong positive or negative signature neighbor among other perturbations.
Extreme absolute logFC rows for Safe_target_23 are statistically unsupported and do not define a pathway.
No high-count cell class escaped the null pattern, while the weakest cell classes remain low-power negatives.
No on-target transcript, pathway, protein complex, disease family, or drug axis can be assigned to the literal Safe_target_28 label.
The apparent cell-type scope is coverage-limited, not a Safe_target_28-selective neuronal phenotype.
Safe_target_29 did not trigger an FDR-supported p53, apoptosis, heat-shock, or immediate-early stress program.
The apparent Safe_target_30 footprint is sampling-limited to six of the 23 subclasses represented in the parquet.
Safe_target_30 did not produce a detectable Trp53/p53 stress response in the measured mouse-brain subclasses.
Full-signature comparisons found no strong positive or negative perturbation neighbor for Safe_target_37 in the tested cell types.
The apparent cell-type restriction of Safe_target_39 is dominated by sampling rather than a strong cell-intrinsic phenotype.
Safe_target_3 did not activate a recurrent p53, DNA-damage, immediate-early, or heat-shock module.
Safe_target_40 did not measurably induce a p53/DNA-damage transcriptional panel.
In the strongest nominal context, Safe_target_40 lacked strong positive or negative signature neighbors.
Safe_target_44 belongs to a 100-member Safe_target control family, making other Safe_target controls the meaningful comparator set rather than paralogs, complexes, receptors, or disease-family genes.
Assignment to Safe_target_46 was not accompanied by induction of a p53/DNA-damage transcript module in the assayed cell types.
Five cell types had no Safe_target_46 DE rows and should be treated as untested rather than buffered or negative.
Selected p53/DNA-damage sentinels were not induced after Safe_target_49 despite literature showing that Cas9 editing can activate p53 responses in other systems.
Safe_target_4 is not interpretable as a measured gene knockdown because no Safe_target_4 transcript row was present and the label did not resolve as an exact mouse gene symbol.
Top signature neighbors did not converge strongly with Safe_target_50 in cortical, Pvalb, thalamic, or midbrain classes.
Safe_target_52 had no measured target transcript and no database-supported mouse-gene identity under this name.
Tubb4a transcript knockdown is repeatedly detectable but is usually transcriptionally buffered, with only 12 FDR-significant rows across 371818 target rows.
151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut is the clearest downstream exception: it has the strongest Tubb4a depletion and the only genome-wide non-target hit, Por down-regulation.
Several assayed neuronal classes had weak or absent on-target depletion and therefore provide little evidence for downstream Tubb4a biology.

The strongest thalamic Tubb4a signature has exploratory same-direction and opposite-direction neighbors, but those neighbors were not tubulin-family perturbations in the restricted 12-gene calculation.

The dataset models reduced Tubb4a transcript in neuronal classes, whereas the best-established TUBB4A disorders are dominant variant syndromes, so the buffered knockdown signature should not be treated as a full HLD6 or DYT4 model.
Safe_target_57 is not a measured endogenous transcript and exact NCBI Gene lookup found no Mus musculus gene symbol for it.
Safe_target_57 had no strong positive or negative signature neighbor among 36,340 same-cell-type perturbation comparisons.
Safe_target_73 was not an outlier among the 100 Safe_target controls.
On-target transcript engagement is not quantifiable for Safe_target_73.
Recurring nominal Safe_target_76 genes are sparse and directionally inconsistent, so they do not define a coherent downstream pathway.
A score-space signature-neighbor check in 110 CNU-HYa HY MM Glut found only weak positive and negative correlations to other perturbations.
The nominal tails do not define a convincing Safe_target_78-sensitive cell class.
Safe_target_78 lacks a recurrent downstream gene module across cell classes.
Safe_target_79 stays null even in the thalamic class where two other Safe_target guides have tiny adjusted-significant signatures.
Safe_target_7 did not induce a canonical p53 or DNA-damage stress panel.
No Safe_target_80 cell-type-selective phenotype was supported.
Safe_target_80 did not produce an overt generic Cas9-cutting artifact in the assayed neuronal classes.
The three highest-cell-count Safe_target_82 comparisons were also FDR-null.
Nominal Safe_target_82 tails did not recur with consistent direction across cell types.
Safe_target_86 did not activate a corrected p53/DNA-damage-response signature despite literature showing that CRISPR-Cas9 editing can activate p53 in some human cell-culture contexts.
Safe_target_87 does not show an individually significant p53 or DNA-damage sentinel-gene response.
Nominally recurrent genes did not form a reproducible Safe_target_89 module.
Safe_target_89 did not induce an FDR-supported p53/DNA-damage response despite the generic possibility of Cas9-induced DNA-break signaling.
Safe_target_94 did not trigger a detectable p53, DNA-damage, or immediate-early stress marker program.
Restricted signature-neighbor analysis did not find a robust real perturbation that phenocopied Safe_target_94.
The Safe_target_96 null is not explained by a global inability to detect DE in its four assayed cell classes.
Safe_target_96 should be treated as an empirical control label rather than as a disease gene, protein-complex member, pathway node, or drug target.
Even the best-powered Safe_target_97 stratum, 151 TH Prkcd Grin2c Glut, remained buffered with zero FDR-significant genes.
This negative scRNA-seq signature should not be generalized into guide- or locus-level nuclease safety.
Slc6a5 perturbation did not significantly deplete the Slc6a5 transcript in any assayed cell class.
The only FDR-significant Slc6a5 downstream response was a three-gene Ppat/Foxg1/Ltk signature in 007 L2-3 IT CTX Glut.
Twenty-one Slc6a5-tested cell classes showed no adjusted-p<0.05 genes.
The Slc6a5 L2/3 Perturb-seq response was uncoupled from the canonical presynaptic glycinergic hyperekplexia pathway.
The dataset does not provide an engaged Slc6a5 model for judging GlyT2 inhibition or safety.
Prkaca and Prkar1a perturbations were effectively knocked down but produced target-transcript-only responses at FDR < 0.10.
The strongest Smo cell type had no meaningful genome-wide positive or inverse signature neighbor.

The dataset gives no support for therapeutically lowering Syt14; the assayed perturbation did not measurably lower Syt14, while prior genetics points to lower SYT14 expression and Syt14 depletion as potentially deleterious.

Tcf12 perturbation produced an apparent pan-assay buffered or undetected response: the target transcript trended down only weakly and no gene reached FDR significance in any of the 22 measured cell types.
217 P MY Pineal Glut was the only cell type with a visibly enriched nominal Tcf12 tail, but the signal was low-powered and entirely non-FDR-significant.

The negative neuronal Tcf12 signature should not be read as loss-of-function safety: human TCF12 haploinsufficiency is tied to craniosynostosis and Kallmann/GnRH biology, while Tcf12 remained uncoupled from Twist1/Twist2 in the assayed neuronal classes.
Across the full mouse-brain panel, Tcf4 target-transcript depletion and broad downstream FDR responses were weak.
Oprd1 is an exploratory Pvalb biomarker of Tcf4 perturbation and a downstream GPCR axis, not a direct TCF4 rescue target.
Thap11, Ogt, and E2f1 did not phenocopy Thap1 in shared neuronal cell types despite representing the available THAP-family, HCF-1/OGT, and pRB/E2F-related comparators.
A restricted scan of all perturbations on high-absolute-score Thap1 genes found no strong positive or negative signature neighbor.
Tmem63b guide cells show reproducible target-transcript depletion but an exceptionally sparse downstream transcriptional response.
Caln1 in L5 extratelencephalic neurons and Fdft1 in hypothalamic GABA neurons are the only non-target genes approaching experiment-wide significance.
The strongest direct Tmem63b knockdown occurred in thalamic, midbrain, hindbrain, and hypothalamic populations, yet those engaged populations were still transcriptionally buffered.
The perturbation models reduced Tmem63b expression, not the gain-of-function/leak-channel state reported for human TMEM63B developmental and epileptic encephalopathy.
Strong Tmem63b knockdown was itself largely buffered, with only Caln1 in 022 L5 ET CTX Glut passing FDR outside the target transcript.
Tuba1a transcript depletion after Tuba1a perturbation was FDR-significant in only 7 of 21 measured brain cell types.
Ndufs4 was an isolated non-tubulin FDR hit in Tubb2a-perturbed Pvalb interneurons.
Tubb4b depletion is reproducible but FDR-significant in only five of the 22 neuronal cell types in which the target transcript was measured.
Even where Tubb4b itself was significantly depleted, downstream transcriptome remodeling was buffered to below FDR detection.
Some assayed cell types provide little evidence for effective Tubb4b loss, including nearly absent engagement in 059 CNU-LGE LSX GABA and a low-count, non-FDR 217 P MY Pineal Glut result.
The quiet neuronal knockdown phenotype is more consistent with context- and allele-specific TUBB4B biology than with a universal transcriptional response to reduced Tubb4b RNA.
Neither selected neurodevelopmental transcription factors nor the whole perturbation panel contained a strong same-cell Zbtb18 signature neighbor.
Human ZBTB18 haploinsufficiency disease genetics should not be read directly from this mostly RNA-gain, FDR-sparse Perturb-seq signature.
Known ZNF423 ciliopathy biology was not expressed as a broad canonical NPHP/Joubert transcriptional module in the neuronal Perturb-seq response.
The striatal/LGE class failed to reveal a Zfp521-centered EBF/BMP-SMAD or Zfp423 module.
The Dbh/monoamine phenotype reported in Zfp521-deficient mouse brain was not reproduced as a cell-autonomous Dbh response in the represented Zfp521 Perturb-seq classes.
The mouse-brain mRNA phenotype did not recover a CTCF/TAD-boundary-like Zfp654 signature.
Rlf and Zfp292 did not phenocopy Zfp654 despite the shared Rlf/292/654 family annotation.
Existing ZHX3 disease literature is context-dependent, and this dataset offers no robust mouse-brain biomarker or direction-of-effect signature for therapeutic extrapolation.
The assayed Zmym2 transcript was not detectably depleted in any tested cell type, including the class with a downstream FDR signature.
Active chromatin-reader and remodeler perturbations in 151 did not reproduce the Zmym2 24-gene cassette.
The neuronal Zmym2 phenotype should not be conflated with ZMYM2-FGFR1 fusion-kinase biology.
